operators.name: view_as_complex
semantics: Corresponds to reference statement x = torch.view_as_complex(x) with input shape [16,2048,128,2].
No bias, no broadcasting, no reduction; only view reinterpretation of the last dimension as complex numbers.
Preserves original memory layout and strides; output is complex64 tensor of shape [16,2048,128].
Implementation should be a simple custom kernel copying data with no arithmetic.

operators.name: multihead_attention
semantics: Corresponds to reference statement output, _ = self.multihead_attn(query, key, value) where self.multihead_attn is nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim=256, num_heads=8, kdim=256, vdim=256, batch_first=True).
Computes multi-head attention with default options: need_weights=True, attn_mask=None, key_padding_mask=None, average_attn_weights=True, is_causal=False.
Bias: in_proj_bias is used in the input projection; out_proj_bias in the output projection.
The input projection is applied as a single linear transformation to query, key, value concatenated (or equivalent batched computation).
Attention scores are computed as q @ k.transpose(-2,-1) / sqrt(head_dim), softmax over last dimension, then weighted sum of values.
Output is projected to embed_dim=256.
The attention weights tensor is computed but discarded in the returned tuple; only the output tensor is used.
The implementation must produce the exact same output as PyTorch's MultiheadAttention with the supplied trained parameters.
All tensor parameters must be on CUDA and float32; input tensors may have strides but should be handled correctly.
Input x is a real float32 tensor of shape [16,2048,128,2] on CUDA.
Converts the last dimension (size 2) into a complex number, producing a complex64 tensor of shape [16,2048,128].
No arithmetic; just reinterpretation of memory.
The result is unused in the rest of the forward, but checkpoint requires it.
Computes multi-head attention as described in the operator contract.
The function returns a tuple (output, attention_weights), but only output is captured.
The checkpoint value is the full tuple containing the output tensor and the attention weight tensor of shape [16,2048,2048] (even though attention weights are not used).
Output tensor shape [16,2048,256] float32 on CUDA.
Returns the output tensor from the attention computation.
Identical to the first element of step_002 tuple.
